- When sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peaks, especially in early 30d window.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or volatile, model often underestimates or fails to capture sharp drops; increase early forecast sensitivity to recent lows.
- Model frequently over-anticipates sharp spikes (e.g., >2.0) and then overshoots — cap forecast peaks at 2.5x recent high or 3.0x recent mean if sentiment is bullish.
- If sentiment shifts from bullish to bearish mid-period, model often fails to adjust — apply a “mean reversion” correction: reduce forecast by 15–30% in 10–15d horizon if sentiment drops below 0.33.
- For 30d forecasts, if true outcome shows rapid decline after a spike, model often lags — adjust by adding 1–2 days of downward trend in forecast if sentiment turns negative.
- If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and history shows mean-reverting behavior, model tends to overpredict — apply a 10–20% downward bias to forecast mean.
